Naming the index $i$ resolves it to the imaginary unit first, not a fresh bound variable
wolfram.note: Wolfram's `{i, ...}` binds `i` as a local dummy that shadows the built-in `I`; ours has no such shadowing, so a Wolfram example naming its index `i` collides with our imaginary unit. Renaming the index avoids it.
